newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK activists to sail to disupted islands next week.
newsitem.headline: HK activists to sail to disupted islands next week.

text.p: Hong Kong activists said on Saturday they would sail to disputed islands in the East China Sea next week to "reclaim" them from the Japanese.

The Action Committee for Defending the Diaoyu Islands said it had bought a 21-metre (69 ft) vessel for HK$500,000 (US$65,000) to sail to the rocky outcrops between Taiwan and Japan's Okinawa island chain.
"This ship will sail forward just like the determination of our activists, who will not bow to pressure from any government," group leader Albert Ho told a news conference.
He said it would take three days for the dozen activists to arrive at the islands, known as Diaoyu in China and Senkakus in Japan. China, Japan and Taiwan all claim ownership of them.
The group earlier this week called off a planned trip to the isles from Taiwan because of a shortage of funds and pressure from the Taiwanese government.

The island sovereignty issue has lit nationalist passions in Chinese communities in both Taiwan and Hong Kong, which reverts to Beijing's control at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.

Hong Kong activists have staged fresh protest marches and demonstrations outside Japan's consulate after several Japanese nationalists landed recently on the islands. Last year, a Japanese rightwing group built a lighthouse on one of them.

The proposed trip to the disputed islands would be the third by anti-Japanese activists from Hong Kong. Last September, a Hong Kong activist drowned when he jumped into stormy water near the islands to press China's claim.
